caption: Field write: each pixel's heat stored for the next frame - flames that rise because each frame builds on the last
why: Field reads numbers remembered from the frame before; Field write is what remembers them. Every frame each pixel works out its new number - heat, water, how much sand - and Field write stores it, to be read back by a Field next frame.

Without it there is no memory and no simulation: each frame would start from nothing. Its neighbours: the Output stores the colour (which Previous reads back); Field write stores a number of your own, invisible until you choose to show it.
steps: **value** is this pixel's new heat: the heat read from the pixel below last frame (a **Field** at `v` plus 0.07), cooled by a **Multiply** at 0.86, with new sparks in the bottom row added by a **Max**.
**field** is 0: the same field the Field node reads, so next frame's read finds what is written now.
The same number also goes to a **Colour ramp** (a fire) and the **Output**, so what is stored and what is shown agree.
Each frame builds on the one before: the bottom row's sparks are written, read one row higher next frame, written there, and so on - the heat climbs.

try.label: Another field
try.text: field 1: the heat is now written somewhere the Field node does not read, so nothing rises - write and read must use the same field.

try.label: Taller flames
try.text: the cooling Multiply at 0.95: less is lost per row, so more of the heat that is written survives to be read further up.

try.label: More sparks
try.text: the Sparkle's density at 0.8: nearly the whole bottom row is lit each frame, so a solid wall of flame rises.
